decisions.choice: Encode a deterministic store-plus-attempt invoice reference into Authorize.net invoiceNumber and refId within the 20-character limit: 8-hex SHA-256 store tag, a single '.', then the Commerce attempt id (max 11 chars). Characters are limited to Authorize.net-safe [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Creation fails closed on overflow or invalid chars (never truncate). After HMAC-SHA512 verification, receiveAuthorizeNetWebhook parses the reference and rejects (no transactionId write, no wake/alarm, no paid lookup) when the store tag does not match the URL siteId and the stored attempt site. Malformed or legacy bare attempt ids are rejected with no writes. A signed webhook still never marks paid; only authoritative getTransactionDetails lookup does.

decisions.choice: 'Place a test order' completes when, for the store's current payment connection (provider, receiving account and binding), Payments' own Stripe or Authorize.net lookup confirmed a TEST checkout as paid and Commerce acknowledged that checkout's payment notice, which Commerce does only after saving the paid order bound to it. Payments records each provider-confirmed paid TEST checkout when a lookup first returns paid; notice receipt and Commerce's acknowledgement are read from the existing payment-notice records, never from a webhook or browser return alone. Authenticated /v1/status adds testOrder {provider, total, paidAt, state: awaiting_notice | awaiting_commerce | recorded} only when such evidence exists, preferring a recorded checkout over the newest paid one. The setup page's strict reader accepts it only in TEST mode with a binding and a matching provider. The step names the provider, amount and paid time (UTC), says what it is waiting for, and is complete only when recorded. No Commerce change, order number or new route. The overall result stays Not ready to sell while Payments runs only in TEST mode. Deploy the Worker together with the matching setup page build.

decisions.choice: Payments hosts a shared 'playground' tenant (site id and binding ref 'playground') bound to the dedicated Stripe sandbox account acct_1UPn3tAq51efiBsg through the STRIPE_PLAYGROUND_SECRET_KEY secret binding, which must be sk_test_ and otherwise fails closed with stripe_mode_mismatch. decisions.choice: Wording and status mapping only. decisions.choice: Returning to the status page after DinkusKit's Approve finishes the sign-in on page load and reads payment status in the same request, so the banner shows the real connection (for example 'Connected: Stripe test mode') with no extra press. Continue pressed before DinkusKit's poll interval waits it out (at most 10 seconds) and then checks, and a check DinkusKit has not approved yet says the approval is not recorded. When the page's own 5-minute DinkusKit sign-in has lapsed for the same admin and store, the page shows the last status that admin read, labelled 'Last checked <time>', with Sign in again; other admins still see 'Payment status not checked' (037). When Payments refuses Stripe setup with merchant_country_required or payments_service_unconfigured (both create nothing), the page names that reason and says no Stripe account was created; any other refusal stays 'not confirmed'. When Stripe needs more information (connection evidence action_required), the step points the owner to Set up or resume Stripe, whose Stripe page lists what is missing, then Check connection; naming the requirement on the page is out of scope. No change to the pass lifetime, the store key, hosted routes, connection evidence, checkout or the ten-bridge-call budget.
